6.3 Procedure 6.3.1 Weigh 0'500 g of sample (see 3.2 ) into a 30 ml nickel crucible. Add 4 g of sodium peroxide and mix thoroughly by means of a Remove any sample powder thin glass rod. adhering to the rod by stirring about 1 g sodium Gently heat the covered peroxide with it. crucible to dull red heat and swirl the melt to Keep in ensure rapid completion of reaction. Allow to molten state for around ten minutes. cool and place the crucible with contents in a 400-ml beaker containing around 50 ml water. Cover the beaker with a watch glass and allow the solidified mass to react with water. Wash the crucible and lid into the beaker and remove these out. Dilute to around 100 ml and Cool and continue boiling for ten minutes. filter through Whatman filter paper 540 with pulp, washing the residue well with hot water. Keep the filtrate (A) aside. 6.3.2 Acidify the filtrate with dilute sulphuric acid, boil, cool and make up to 250 ml in a volumetric flask. 6.3.3 Take a suitable aliquot containing about 50 mg of chromium in a beaker, add 15 ml of ( 0'8 percent ) silver nitrate solution, 2 drops of ( 2 percent ) potassium permanganate solution, and 10 ml of ( 25 percent ) ammonium persulphate solution, boil the solution for 10 minutes to oxidize chromium and manganese and to destroy excess of persulphate. Add 0'5 percent sodium nitrite solution drop by drop to boiling potassium reduction of solution till the permanganate solution and subsequent decomposition of any precipitated manganese dioxide Add 1 g and then add 1 to 2 drops in excess. of urea and stir to dissolve. Cool the solution. Add 50 ml of 0'1 N ferrous ammonium sulphate solution. Shake up and add 115 ml of sulphuricphosphoric acid mixture. Dilute to around 200 ml with water, add three drops of sodium diphenylamine sulphonate indicator solution and titrate it slowly with standard 0'1 N potassium dichromate solution stirring constantly until the green colour begins to darken. Continue the titration slowly till a drop of dichromate solution gives a permanent violet-blue coloration. Note the titre value. 6.3.4

Blank

Take 50 ml of 0'1 N ferrous ammonium sulphate solution in a 250 ml conical flask. Add acid mixture and dilute to 20 ml. Add few drops of sodium diphenylamine sulphonate indicator solution and titrate with standard 0'1 N potassium dichromate solution as above to a permanent violet-blue end point. 6.4 Calculation &4--B) ~0'002534~ c 1oo
